title: Inner Monologues with Ethan Kross, PhD

sentences.en: Stop what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 停下你手头的事。

sentences.en: Quick, recall your childhood phone number.
sentences.zh: 快，回想一下你小时候的电话号码。

sentences.en: Done?
sentences.zh: 想到了吗？

sentences.en: Okay, so did you say the numbers inside your head?
sentences.zh: 好，那么你是用脑子里的声音念出这些数字的吗？

sentences.en: Did the phone number appear as an image?
sentences.zh: 还是说电话号码是以图像的形式出现的？

sentences.en: Something else?
sentences.zh: 或者是其他形式？

sentences.en: You may be wondering why I'm asking you this seemingly off-the-wall question.
sentences.zh: 你可能在想，我为什么要问你这个看似突兀的问题。

sentences.en: Well, it's because I'm trying to get you to analyze your inner voice.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是因为我想让你分析一下自己的内心独白。

sentences.en: You may have heard about the internet debate recently on inner monologues.
sentences.zh: 你可能最近在网上听说过关于内心独白的争论。

sentences.en: It all started from a tweet that went viral.
sentences.zh: 这一切始于一条疯传的推文。

sentences.en: That tweet said that some people have an internal narrative and some don't.
sentences.zh: 那条推文说，有些人有内心独白，而有些人没有。

sentences.en: What ensued were thousands of comments, retweets, and news stories on the topic.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是成千上万条评论、转发和关于这个话题的新闻报道。

sentences.en: Turns out that people have a lot to say about their inner voices.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，人们对于自己的内心声音有很多话要说。

sentences.en: Some people were shocked to learn that there are those who have a running commentary in their heads all the time, while others don't have a permanent live-in narrator.
sentences.zh: 有些人很震惊地发现，原来有人脑子里一直有旁白，而另一些人并没有一个常驻的内心叙述者。

sentences.en: According to our guest for this episode, University of Michigan psychology professor Dr. Ethan Cross, it's not exactly that simple.
sentences.zh: 据我们本期的嘉宾，密歇根大学心理学教授伊森·克罗斯博士（Dr. Ethan Cross）所说，事情并没有那么简单。

sentences.en: He says every healthy person has an inner voice, but how it manifests can vary dramatically from person to person.
sentences.zh: 他说每个健康的人都有内心声音，但它表现出来的方式因人而异。

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, a bi-weekly podcast from the American Psychological Association that explores the connections between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》（Speaking of Psychology），这是美国心理学会推出的一档双周播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm your host, Caitlin Luna.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人凯特琳·卢纳（Caitlin Luna）。

sentences.en: Dr. Cross is joining us via Skype from Ann Arbor, Michigan.
sentences.zh: 克罗斯博士正通过Skype从密歇根州安娜堡市与我们连线。

sentences.en: Welcome, Dr. Cross.
sentences.zh: 欢迎您，克罗斯博士。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: First, I want to establish what an inner monologue or inner voice is.
sentences.zh: 首先，我想明确一下什么是内心独白或内心声音。

sentences.en: How do you describe it?
sentences.zh: 您是如何描述它的？

sentences.en: So I think of the inner voice as silent verbal processing.
sentences.zh: 我认为内心声音是一种无声的语言处理过程。

sentences.en: So the example you gave to begin the podcast was a really good one.
sentences.zh: 你刚才在节目开头举的例子就非常好。

sentences.en: So if I asked you to silently repeat a phone number in your head, that would be you activating your inner voice, so to speak, at a very basic level.
sentences.zh: 如果你让我默默地在脑子里重复一个电话号码，那可以说就是你在激活自己的内心声音，处于一个非常基础的层面。

sentences.en: So you're using verbal reasoning skills to play with information.
sentences.zh: 所以你是在利用语言推理能力来处理信息。

sentences.en: And there are, of course, all sorts of ways that we can use internal silent language to help navigate our lives.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们还有各种各样的方法利用内在的无声语言来帮助我们驾驭生活。

sentences.en: So we can and often do use that verbal reasoning to keep information in mind,
sentences.zh: 我们可以，而且经常使用这种语言推理来记住信息，

sentences.en: like when we rehearse a phone number or when we might silently rehearse what we're going to say in a given context.
sentences.zh: 比如当我们背诵电话号码，或者在特定场合默默排练我们要说的话时。

sentences.en: So if I'm preparing for a presentation, I might repeat something over and over, how I'm going to open the talk.
sentences.zh: 如果我要准备一场演讲，我可能会一遍又一遍地重复我该如何开场。

sentences.en: But we also use language, silent language, the inner voice, so to speak, to do lots of other things, to imagine how we might respond to different situations in our future.
sentences.zh: 但我们也利用语言，这种无声的语言，也就是所谓的内心声音，来做许多其他事情，比如想象我们未来在不同情况下会如何应对。

sentences.en: Some people report having conversations with themselves silently, like you might see, you know, often popularized in movies, oh, my God, what am I going to do if this happens?
sentences.zh: 有些人报告说会默默地和自己对话，就像你在电影里经常看到的那样，天哪，如果发生这种情况我该怎么办？

sentences.en: Well, if this happens, I'll do that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果发生这种情况，我就那样做。

sentences.en: And so the inner voice can take on lots of different roles, depending on the different context we find ourselves in.
sentences.zh: 所以，根据我们所处的不同环境，内心声音可以扮演许多不同的角色。

sentences.en: So how can those inner voices vary from person to person?
sentences.zh: 那么，这些内心声音在不同人之间会有什么差异呢？

sentences.en: As you said, every healthy person has an inner voice, but just how it appears is different.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，每个健康的人都有内心声音，但它出现的方式各不相同。

sentences.en: Yeah, so that's a great question.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, going back to the tweet, the different reactions that people had, what was so interesting to me about those with some people saying, oh,
sentences.zh: 我想，回到那条推文，人们的不同反应，最让我感兴趣的是有些人说，哦，

sentences.en: I never talk to myself.
sentences.zh: 我从不和自己说话。

sentences.en: I don't have an inner voice.
sentences.zh: 我没有内心声音。

sentences.en: And other people saying, oh, I talk to myself all the time.
sentences.zh: 而另一些人说，哦，我一直在和自己说话。

sentences.en: I'm always engaged in some kind of inner monologue.
sentences.zh: 我总是沉浸在某种内心独白中。

sentences.en: I think part of the issue there is that people have different conceptions of what the inner voice actually is.
sentences.zh: 我认为部分问题在于，人们对内心声音到底是什么有不同的理解。

sentences.en: So in my mind, the inner voice covers all the terrain we just discussed, ranging from activities where you are silently rehearsing what you're trying to memorize or say.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，内心声音涵盖了我们刚才讨论的所有领域，从你默默排练试图记忆或表达的内容的活动，

sentences.en: That's one manifestation of the inner voice.
sentences.zh: 这是内心声音的一种表现形式。

sentences.en: But another manifestation at the other end of the spectrum might be something like internal rumination, where we're engaged.
sentences.zh: 但在光谱的另一端，另一种表现形式可能是某种内在的沉思，我们沉浸其中。

sentences.en: Oh, my God, what should I do?
sentences.zh: 天哪，我该怎么办？

sentences.en: How is this going to happen?
sentences.zh: 这会怎么发生？

sentences.en: What if this happens?
sentences.zh: 如果发生这种情况怎么办？

sentences.en: What if the coronavirus affects my family, to use a current event?
sentences.zh: 用当下的事件来说，如果新冠病毒影响了我的家人怎么办？

sentences.en: That's a different manifestation of the inner voice.
sentences.zh: 那是内心声音的另一种表现形式。

sentences.en: And I do think it is the case that some people engage in that kind of inner rumination a lot more than other people.
sentences.zh: 我的确认为，有些人确实比其他人更多地进行那种内心沉思。

sentences.en: Some people report not ruminating at all about things.
sentences.zh: 有些人报告说根本不会对事情进行沉思。

sentences.en: And if you are equating the inner voice with a kind of ruminative thought process, then, yeah, there's going to be huge variability in the degree to which people engage it.
sentences.zh: 如果你把内心声音等同于一种沉思的思维过程，那么，是的，人们参与其中的程度会有巨大的差异。

sentences.en: But if you go to the other end of the spectrum and look at the basic functions that the inner voice serves when it comes to memorizing information,
sentences.zh: 但如果你走到光谱的另一端，看看内心声音在记忆信息时所起的基本功能，

sentences.en: keeping information active in your mind, then I think it is a universal that characterizes all, quote, unquote, normal, healthy, functioning individuals.
sentences.zh: 即保持信息在脑海中活跃，那么我认为这是一个普遍特征，适用于所有所谓的“正常、健康、功能正常”的个体。

sentences.en: So what are your thoughts about how this discussion just, you know, exploded on the Internet?
sentences.zh: 那么，对于这场讨论在互联网上突然“爆发”，您有什么看法？

sentences.en: Are you surprised by that?
sentences.zh: 您感到惊讶吗？

sentences.en: Or, you know, what are your thoughts?
sentences.zh: 或者说，您有什么想法？

sentences.en: I think it's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这很迷人。

sentences.en: I think the inner voice is such an interesting topic because I think it is very salient to so many people.
sentences.zh: 我认为内心声音是一个非常有趣的话题，因为它对很多人来说都非常突出。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But it's an incredibly private experience.
sentences.zh: 但它是一种极其私密的体验。

sentences.en: So many people spend a lot of time in their heads.
sentences.zh: 很多人花大量时间在自己的脑子里。

sentences.en: By some estimates, we spend most of our waking hours thinking and verbally reflecting on our lives internally.
sentences.zh: 据估计，我们大部分清醒的时间都在进行思考，并在内心对生活进行语言上的反思。

sentences.en: And so it's something that many people are doing so frequently, but they're not necessarily talking about it with others.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是许多人经常做的事情，但他们不一定会与他人谈论。

sentences.en: It's not as though I go meet some friends for coffee.
sentences.zh: 并不是说我出去和朋友喝咖啡时会说，

sentences.en: Hey, guess what I was just talking to myself about?
sentences.zh: 嘿，猜猜我刚才在和自己说什么？

sentences.en: And so so it's this it's very, very common, intimate experience we have, yet we don't talk about it very much.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一种非常非常普遍、亲密的体验，但我们却很少谈论它。

sentences.en: And when you look at the science, it's often coded with jargon, working memory, the phonological loop,
sentences.zh: 当你审视科学时，它通常被术语所掩盖，比如工作记忆、语音回路，

sentences.en: which is the technical term that describes the component of working memory that is verbal, linguistic in nature.
sentences.zh: 这是描述工作记忆中本质上是语言性的、文字性的那个组成部分的专业术语。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Really complicated, jargon filled scientific terMs.
sentences.zh: 非常复杂、充满术语的科学词汇。

sentences.en: And so I think once there was a an opportunity to have a public conversation about this topic,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，一旦有了公开讨论这个话题的机会，

sentences.en: many people were excited to participate and they were particularly excited to participate when something somewhat counterintuitive was was raised.
sentences.zh: 许多人都很兴奋地参与其中，尤其是当提出一些有些反直觉的事情时，他们就更兴奋了。

sentences.en: The idea that some people don't have an internal monologue.
sentences.zh: 即有些人没有内心独白这一观点。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it just brings up that, you know, everyone wants to share their personal perspective and like, oh, I always think this way.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这只是引出了每个人都想分享自己的个人观点，比如，哦，我总是这样思考。

sentences.en: I mean, for me, I have an internal narrator all the time, so I know what that camp feels like.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对我来说，我一直有一个内在的叙述者，所以我知道那个阵营的感觉。

sentences.en: But yeah, I had a conversation with someone recently who was asking me about some of this research and this person was saying, I work at home alone.
sentences.zh: 但是，我最近和一个人谈话，他问我一些关于这项研究的问题，那个人说，我在家独自工作。

sentences.en: This was a web designer and he was saying, all I do is talk to myself all the time in my head.
sentences.zh: 这是一个网页设计师，他说，我所做的就是一直在脑子里和自己说话。

sentences.en: That's just my life.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的生活。

sentences.en: And so it was so that the notion that that reality might not characterize other people's experiences was a, to use the technical term,
sentences.zh: 所以，那种认为这种现实可能并不代表其他人体验的观念，用专业术语来说，

sentences.en: a mind blower for that for that for that person.
sentences.zh: 对那个人来说简直是“震撼心灵”。

sentences.en: And so I think that's what we saw happen on Twitter surrounding this conversation.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这就是我们在推特上围绕这场对话所看到的情况。

sentences.en: So, you know, how is this different from people who hear voices?
sentences.zh: 那么，这与听到声音的人有什么不同呢？

sentences.en: I mean, the hearing voices is often associated with serious mental illness like schizophrenia.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，听到声音通常与精神分裂症等严重的精神疾病有关。

sentences.en: So can you differentiate between what we mean by internal monologue and hearing voices?
sentences.zh: 所以您能区分我们所说的内心独白和听到声音吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a great question.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: And there are a couple of distinctions worth noting.
sentences.zh: 有几个区别值得注意。

sentences.en: So oftentimes when we're talking about the inner voice, I'm talking about the awareness that verbal processing is occurring, but that I can, so, you know,
sentences.zh: 通常当我们谈论内心声音时，我指的是意识到语言处理正在发生，但我可以，你知道，

sentences.en: when I repeat a phone number, my child's phone number, I can, I have the subjective experience of using language to repeat that number.
sentences.zh: 当我重复一个电话号码，我孩子的电话号码时，我可以，我有使用语言来重复那个数字的主观体验。

sentences.en: I'm not just seeing it, I'm internally hearing those words.
sentences.zh: 我不仅仅是看到它，我还在内心听到了那些词。

sentences.en: But I know that the source of that quote unquote inner voice is me, right?
sentences.zh: 但我知道那个所谓的“内心声音”的来源是我，对吧？

sentences.en: I don't think that the voice is coming from some other external entity like the government or aliens and so forth.
sentences.zh: 我不认为那个声音来自政府或外星人等其他外部实体。

sentences.en: So that's the first distinction worth noting that typically when we're talking about the inner voice, we usually,
sentences.zh: 所以这是第一个值得注意的区别，通常当我们谈论内心声音时，我们通常，

sentences.en: we know where it's coming from and it's usually ourselves and has this abstract quality to it.
sentences.zh: 我们知道它来自哪里，通常是我们自己，并且它具有这种抽象的特质。

sentences.en: Now, that's not to say that we're not capable of hearing other voices too.
sentences.zh: 现在，这并不是说我们没有能力听到其他声音。

sentences.en: So many people, if I asked you to imagine your mother telling you to clean up your room right now,
sentences.zh: 很多人，如果我让你想象你母亲现在让你打扫房间，

sentences.en: you could probably simulate that experience and actually hear your mother's voice in your head or some approximation of it.
sentences.zh: 你可能能够模拟那种体验，并真切地在脑海中听到你母亲的声音或某种近似的声音。

sentences.en: And so that would be you hearing your mom and so we can hear other voices.
sentences.zh: 所以那将是你听到你妈妈的声音，所以我们可以听到其他声音。

sentences.en: But again, typically, you know that the voice is coming from, you are the source of your mom's voice.
sentences.zh: 但同样，通常你知道声音来自哪里，你是你妈妈声音的来源。

sentences.en: It's not your mom implanting herself in your head and controlling you.
sentences.zh: 并不是你妈妈植入你的脑海并在控制你。

sentences.en: And so when we get into mental illness, this line between knowing the source of the voice, whether it's coming from me or the external world, that tends to get blurred.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们谈到精神疾病时，这种区分声音来源（是来自我还是外部世界）的界限往往会变得模糊。

sentences.en: And so oftentimes in the case of schizophrenia and other kinds of auditory hallucinations, we are attributing this voice to another agent.
sentences.zh: 因此，在精神分裂症和其他类型的幻听案例中，我们往往将这种声音归因于另一个主体。

sentences.en: Now, I should say there have been studies which ask people, like, do you ever hear voices and believe they come from other sources?
sentences.zh: 现在，我应该说，有一些研究询问人们，比如，你是否曾经听到声音并相信它们来自其他来源？

sentences.en: For example, like God, is the voice in your head delivering a message from God?
sentences.zh: 例如，像上帝，你脑子里的声音是在传递来自上帝的信息吗？

sentences.en: And there are people who do not meet, like, diagnostic criteria for mental illness who do report hearing the voice of God and believing it's coming from somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 确实有一些不符合精神疾病诊断标准的人，他们报告说听到了上帝的声音，并相信它来自其他地方。

sentences.en: So the line between mental illness and normality in this context, it's not cut and dry.
sentences.zh: 所以在这个背景下，精神疾病和正常之间的界限并不是非黑即白的。

sentences.en: There are other elements that go into a diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 还有其他因素会影响诊断。

sentences.en: Does that help give you a sense of the terrain?
sentences.zh: 这能让你对这个领域有个了解吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it does.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实。

sentences.en: And I think I've often heard it's people who have auditory hallucinations.
sentences.zh: 而且我经常听说，对于那些有幻听的人，

sentences.en: It's like as though the person was next to you talking to you as opposed to inside your head.
sentences.zh: 就好像那个人就在你旁边和你说话，而不是在你的脑子里。

sentences.en: Is that correct or is it very?
sentences.zh: 这是正确的吗，还是说情况很复杂？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，是的。

sentences.en: I mean, that captures part of the phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这捕捉到了这种现象的一部分。

sentences.en: And many perfectly normal, healthy individuals experience those kinds of auditory hallucinations at some point in their life.
sentences.zh: 许多完全正常、健康的个体在他们生命中的某个时刻也会经历那种幻听。

sentences.en: And so when we're making diagnoses of mental illness, we're taking into account lots of information, not just the frequency of those kinds of events, but other diagnostic criteria,
sentences.zh: 所以当我们进行精神疾病诊断时，我们会考虑很多信息，不仅仅是这些事件发生的频率，还有其他诊断标准，

sentences.en: too.
sentences.zh: 也是如此。

sentences.en: Okay, so people can rest easy if they have an inner monologue.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以如果人们有内心独白，他们可以放心了。

sentences.en: They're not likely suffering from a serious mental illness.
sentences.zh: 他们不太可能患有严重的精神疾病。

sentences.en: Yeah, if that's the only thing that's – and inner monologue, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，如果这只是——内心独白，是的。

sentences.en: Inner monologue, exactly.
sentences.zh: 内心独白，没错。

sentences.en: We'd all be in big trouble if that were the case.
sentences.zh: 如果真是那样的话，我们都有大麻烦了。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: So are we born with an inner monologue and when does it develop?
sentences.zh: 那么我们是天生就有内心独白吗？它是什么时候发展的？

sentences.en: That's a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: And, you know, there's not a ton of research that looks at this.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，并没有大量的研究关注这一点。

sentences.en: What we do know is that what I've seen, the earliest study I've seen looking at verbal working memory,
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的是，据我所见，我所见过的关于言语工作记忆的最早研究，

sentences.en: which is when we are using language to rehearse information and keeping it fresh in mind, that that capacity, we can see evidence for it at around 18 months of age.
sentences.zh: 也就是当我们使用语言来排练信息并保持其在脑海中新鲜时，这种能力，我们可以在大约18个月大的时候看到证据。

sentences.en: But that's not to say that it doesn't develop earlier.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是说它没有更早发展。

sentences.en: That's simply what we've documented thus far.
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是我们目前所记录到的。

sentences.en: And so relatively early on in the lifespan, although that, you know, of course depends on who you're talking to, but that's the earliest I've seen evidence for this coming online.
sentences.zh: 所以相对较早地出现在生命周期中，尽管这当然取决于你和谁谈论，但这是我所见过的这种能力开始出现的最早证据。

sentences.en: And does it help children develop self-control?
sentences.zh: 它能帮助儿童发展自控力吗？

sentences.en: I think you spoke briefly about that, how a child might be told instructions by a parent and then they might repeat them out loud and it becomes their inner voice,
sentences.zh: 我想你刚才简短地谈到了这一点，孩子可能会被父母告知指令，然后他们可能会大声重复，这变成了他们的内心声音，

sentences.en: maybe to help them regulate their behavior, put away your toys, wash your hands, that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 也许是为了帮助他们调节行为，比如收好玩具、洗手之类的。

sentences.en: Yeah, so this is a really interesting angle on all this work.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以这是所有这些工作中一个非常有趣的角度。

sentences.en: So many psychologists believe that the inner voice is actually central to how we learn to control ourselves.
sentences.zh: 许多心理学家认为，内心声音实际上是我们学习如何控制自己的核心。

sentences.en: And so one of the key ways that we learn self-control is through the interactions we have with our parents, where our parents or caretakers give us instructions.
sentences.zh: 所以我们学习自控的关键方式之一是通过我们与父母的互动，父母或看护人给我们指令。

sentences.en: They tell us what to do and what not to do.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我们该做什么，不该做什么。

sentences.en: So put your toys away and, you know, don't pick your nose at the dinner table.
sentences.zh: 所以把玩具收好，你知道，不要在餐桌上挖鼻孔。

sentences.en: Well, you probably shouldn't pick your nose anywhere, but you get the point.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你可能在任何地方都不应该挖鼻孔，但你明白我的意思。

sentences.en: And if you've ever spent some time around children,
sentences.zh: 如果你曾经花时间陪伴孩子，

sentences.en: what you often see is this really fun and curious and magical kind of event where kids go off on their own and they start talking to themselves, oftentimes out loud to begin with.
sentences.zh: 你经常会看到这种非常有趣、好奇和神奇的现象，孩子们独自走开，开始自言自语，通常一开始是大声说出来的。

sentences.en: They're like giving themselves instructions, right?
sentences.zh: 他们就像是在给自己下指令，对吧？

sentences.en: So like, no, I shouldn't pick my nose at the dinner table or, or yes, I have to go clean my room.
sentences.zh: 比如，不，我不应该在餐桌上挖鼻孔，或者，是的，我必须去打扫我的房间。

sentences.en: And it's, they're essentially repeating what their caretakers are saying, are telling them to do, right?
sentences.zh: 他们本质上是在重复看护人告诉他们要做的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: They're repeating it to themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们在对自己重复这些话。

sentences.en: And the idea is that this is the way in which self-control is, is developing.
sentences.zh: 而这个观点是，这就是自控力发展的方式。

sentences.en: Messages from our caretakers and our culture more generally are getting injected into our own lives and we're rehearsing them as kids out loud.
sentences.zh: 来自我们的看护者以及更广泛的文化信息，正在被注入我们的生活中，我们作为孩子时会大声地重复这些信息。

sentences.en: And what happens is that over time, we don't do that out loud, but that process then goes internal.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，我们不再大声说出来，这个过程就转入内心了。

sentences.en: It becomes a silent inner monologue where we are directing ourselves, so to speak, you know, privately.
sentences.zh: 它变成了一种无声的内心独白，可以说，我们在私下里引导着自己。

sentences.en: And, and that then becomes a tool that some psychologists and scientists, myself included, think that we rely on throughout our lives as a very powerful tool,
sentences.zh: 这进而成为一种工具，包括我在内的一些心理学家和科学家认为，我们一生都在依赖它，这是一个非常强大的工具，

sentences.en: this ability to use language to control ourselves.
sentences.zh: 即利用语言来控制我们自己的能力。

sentences.en: One thing, when I read an interview you did with today.com and you spoke about how you don't necessarily need to hear to have an inner voice.
sentences.zh: 有一件事，当我读到你接受today.com采访时，你谈到一个人不一定需要听力才能拥有内心声音。

sentences.en: You know, I find that interesting because I, I, in a previous life, I worked at Gallaudet University, which is a deaf university.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我觉得这很有趣，因为在过去的生活中，我曾在加劳德特大学工作，那是一所聋人大学。

sentences.en: So I was surrounded by deaf people on campus all the time and have deaf friends and know sign language and all that.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直被校园里的聋人包围，我有聋人朋友，也懂手语等等。

sentences.en: So what you said is that you don't need to have, you know, you don't need to be able to hear to have an inner voice that perhaps maybe a deaf person, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以你所说的是，你不需要拥有，你知道，你不需要有听力也能拥有内心声音，也许聋人，你知道，

sentences.en: sees sign language in their head, sees words, that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 在脑海中看到手语，看到文字，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So can you elaborate on that?
sentences.zh: 那么你能详细说明一下吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there's like a really interesting question, right?
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: If this inner voice is central to, is fundamental to how we live our lives, right?
sentences.zh: 如果这种内心声音对于我们如何生活是核心的、是根本的，对吧？

sentences.en: It's, it's used in all these different capacities.
sentences.zh: 它被用于所有这些不同的能力中。

sentences.en: What happens to people who have impoverished verbal capacities or linguistic capacities?
sentences.zh: 那么那些言语能力或语言能力受损的人会怎样呢？

sentences.en: And so hearing impaired populations are one.
sentences.zh: 听力受损人群就是其中之一。

sentences.en: And so there has been a little bit of work on this that shows, as you just implied, that people who are hearing impaired also report silently talking to themselves, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点已经有一些研究，正如你刚才所暗示的，听力受损的人也报告说他们会无声地自言自语，可以这么说。

sentences.en: And one of the ways in which they report doing so is simply using the same communication channel that they use to communicate with people in their worlds, right?
sentences.zh: 他们报告这样做的方式之一，就是简单地使用他们与周围人交流时所用的同一种沟通渠道，对吧？

sentences.en: So they're engaging in not in inner talking, so verbally, but with inner signing, using seeing signs in their mind as they are engaging in this kind of internal introspection.
sentences.zh: 所以他们参与的不是言语上的内心对话，而是内心手语，在进行这种内心反省时，在脑海中看到手语。

sentences.en: Um, so it's happening, but they're using a different modality to do it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以它确实在发生，但他们使用了不同的方式来做到这一点。

sentences.en: Have you done any research on bilingual people?
sentences.zh: 你做过关于双语者的研究吗？

sentences.en: Like, would a, would a bilingual person have an inner monologue in two languages?
sentences.zh: 比如，双语者会有两种语言的内心独白吗？

sentences.en: Um, you know, I haven't done any work on that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，我还没做过那方面的研究。

sentences.en: Uh, it's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 呃，这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: There is work showing that among bilinguals, the language that you use to reason about experiences can have, in some cases, quite interesting implications for how you think.
sentences.zh: 有研究表明，在双语者中，你用来思考经历的语言，在某些情况下，会对你的思维方式产生相当有趣的影响。

sentences.en: So if you think about an emotional event in your second language, the impact it has on you is blunted, right?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你用第二语言思考一件情绪化的事件，它对你的影响会减弱，对吧？

sentences.en: So it doesn't have the same emotional punch than if you think about it in your native language.
sentences.zh: 所以它不会像用母语思考时那样具有相同的情绪冲击力。

sentences.en: Your native language is the language where you learn swear words and, you know, your first learning, like, your experience of emotion is encoded using your native language.
sentences.zh: 你的母语是你学习脏话的语言，你知道，你最初的学习，比如，你对情绪的体验是用你的母语编码的。

sentences.en: And so the idea is that when you switch to the non-native language, those emotional tags and experiences are stripped away as well.
sentences.zh: 所以观点是，当你切换到非母语时，那些情绪标签和体验也会被剥离。

sentences.en: So, so there's a lot of work in that area.
sentences.zh: 所以，在这个领域有很多研究。

sentences.en: It's also, I think, I speak different languages and it's easy for me to swap into, um,
sentences.zh: 我也认为，我会说不同的语言，如果我想无声地说西班牙语并排练一个数字，我可以很容易地刻意切换到，嗯，

sentences.en: another language deliberately if I want to silently speak Spanish and rehearse a number I can.
sentences.zh: 另一种语言。

sentences.en: So I think that flexibility exists.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这种灵活性是存在的。

sentences.en: The question of when, you know, do people oscillate back and forth?
sentences.zh: 关于人们何时会来回切换的问题，你知道，

sentences.en: That I'm not sure.
sentences.zh: 我不确定。

sentences.en: Or I am aware of some anecdotal reports among people who have studied abroad who tell me that they've begun, they start dreaming in a foreign language.
sentences.zh: 或者我了解一些轶事报道，一些留学生告诉我，他们开始用外语做梦了。

sentences.en: And we do find our inner voice perking up during our dreams, too.
sentences.zh: 我们也发现我们的内心声音在做梦时也会活跃起来。

sentences.en: Our dreams often have verbal information.
sentences.zh: 我们的梦中经常有语言信息。

sentences.en: We process verbally in our dreams, too.
sentences.zh: 我们在梦中也会进行语言处理。

sentences.en: So I think there's some, I think it is likely to occur, but I just don't know of any evidence that has really nailed it.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为有一些，我认为这很可能会发生，但我不知道有什么证据能真正证实这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah, an interesting area that, um, could be studied in the future, for sure.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个有趣的领域，嗯，未来肯定可以研究。

sentences.en: Um, have you done any research about people who talk out loud to themselves?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你做过关于那些大声自言自语的人的研究吗？

sentences.en: You know, we have, so it's a great question that often comes up.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们做过，这是一个经常被问到的好问题。

sentences.en: We haven't touched on, touched this yet.
sentences.zh: 我们还没有涉及这一点。

sentences.en: And, um, I think it's a really interesting topic.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，我认为这是一个非常有趣的话题。

sentences.en: So, uh, in some work we find that, you know, if you talk to yourself in particular in a third person, when you're trying to manage yourself.
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，在一些研究中我们发现，你知道，如果你在试图管理自己时，特别是在用第三人称对自己说话。

sentences.en: So if I've got a really, you know, uh, big presentation, I'm nervous, try to work through my feelings, not in the first one.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我有一个非常，你知道，呃，重要的演讲，我很紧张，试图理清我的感受，不是用第一人称。

sentences.en: Hey, what am I going to say?
sentences.zh: 嘿，我要说什么？

sentences.en: But what is Ethan going to say?
sentences.zh: 而是伊森（Ethan）要说什么？

sentences.en: Why is Ethan nervous?
sentences.zh: 为什么伊森会紧张？

sentences.en: Engaging in that shift from first to third can be, uh, helpful for giving people distance from their experience, making, Hey, it's not about you.
sentences.zh: 从第一人称转变为第三人称，可以帮助人们与自己的经历保持距离，让人们意识到，嘿，这与你无关。

sentences.en: Like it's about someone else and relieving anxiety and improving performance as a result.
sentences.zh: 就像它是关于别人的，从而缓解焦虑并提高表现。

sentences.en: And so some people often ask, well, what if you did that out loud?
sentences.zh: 所以有些人经常问，好吧，如果你大声说出来会怎样？

sentences.en: And my intuition is that it would be likewise beneficial, but, and this is an important, but you can't do it when other people are around you
sentences.zh: 我的直觉是这同样会有益，但是，这是一个重要的“但是”，当周围有其他人时你不能这样做，

sentences.en: because there's a huge social stigma that exists about people talking to themselves out loud that violate social convention quite powerfully.
sentences.zh: 因为社会上对大声自言自语的人存在巨大的偏见，这相当严重地违反了社会公约。

sentences.en: And so you, I think there are other ramifications that that might have for people.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，这可能会给人们带来其他后果。

sentences.en: So the, the short answer to your question, which I just didn't give you is that no, we haven't looked at this out loud,
sentences.zh: 所以，对你问题的简短回答，我刚才没给出的，是：不，我们还没有研究过大声说出来的情况，

sentences.en: but I think my guess is that there are instances, but we know there are instances where people are frustrated
sentences.zh: 但我猜想，确实存在一些情况，我们知道在某些情况下人们会感到沮丧，

sentences.en: and almost to the point of not being able to contain their frustration.
sentences.zh: 几乎到了无法抑制沮丧的地步。

sentences.en: They blurk things out to themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们会对自己脱口而出一些话。

sentences.en: And there's a whole set of interesting questions that surround that behavior that warrant future study.
sentences.zh: 围绕这种行为有一系列有趣的问题，值得未来研究。

sentences.en: So when does your inner model go from being helpful to being self-defeating?
sentences.zh: 那么你的内心模型何时从有帮助变成自我挫败的呢？

sentences.en: So I think that happens when we, you know, we, we often use our inner monologue to solve problems and it can be a really tool,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为当我们，你知道，我们经常使用内心独白来解决问题时，它可能是一个非常有用的工具，

sentences.en: a useful tool for helping us think through, like simulate different possibilities for what might happen and come to a realization about how we should respond or behave or act.
sentences.zh: 一个有用的工具，帮助我们思考，比如模拟可能发生的不同可能性，并意识到我们应该如何回应、表现或行动。

sentences.en: And so super duper useful ability, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个超级有用的能力，对吧？

sentences.en: The ability to simulate and plan and,
sentences.zh: 模拟和计划的能力，以及，

sentences.en: and the inner voice is something that helps us do that in many contexts where I think the inner voice can and does get us into not just trouble,
sentences.zh: 内心声音在许多情境下都能帮助我们做到这一点，但我认为内心声音确实会让我们陷入麻烦，甚至是大麻烦，

sentences.en: but big trouble is when that planning simulation process runs off course as it does when we tend to ruminate or worry excessively or perseverate on negative things in our lives.
sentences.zh: 是在那种计划模拟过程偏离轨道时，就像我们倾向于反刍、过度担忧或对生活中的负面事物纠缠不清时那样。

sentences.en: There, there's a ton of data showing that when we, when we are constantly rehearsing the negative things,
sentences.zh: 有大量数据表明，当我们不断地排练负面事物时，

sentences.en: or what, what, what if this happens and what should I do, or I can't believe I said this and, uh, how am I going to feel?
sentences.zh: 或者“如果发生这种情况怎么办，我该怎么办”，或者“我不敢相信我说了这些，呃，我会有什么感觉？”

sentences.en: And what did that, what if this happens that engaging that kind of cyclical verbal negative dynamic,
sentences.zh: 以及“如果发生这种情况怎么办”，参与那种循环的负面言语动态，

sentences.en: what that does is that it elevates our stress levels and it keeps those stress levels elevated over time.
sentences.zh: 它所做的是提高我们的压力水平，并使这些压力水平随着时间的推移保持在高位。

sentences.en: And that can have strikingly negative implications for many of the things that matter most to us, for example, our health, right?
sentences.zh: 这可能会对我们最看重的许多事情产生显著的负面影响，例如我们的健康，对吧？

sentences.en: So there's a lot of data showing that when we're ruminating and perseverating excessively over negative things in our life,
sentences.zh: 所以有大量数据表明，当我们对生活中的负面事物进行过度的反刍和纠缠时，

sentences.en: that activates our fight or flight response and, and keeps it activated chronically over time.
sentences.zh: 这会激活我们的战斗或逃跑反应，并使其长期保持激活状态。

sentences.en: Not very good.
sentences.zh: 这不太好。

sentences.en: If we're spending all of our time, you know, lost in verbal thought, so to speak, over the negative things in our lives, our ability to, to think and reason is limited.
sentences.zh: 如果我们把所有时间都花在，你知道，沉浸在言语思维中，可以说，思考生活中负面的事情，我们思考和推理的能力就会受到限制。

sentences.en: So what happens if you're spending all your time occupying the limited resources you have for thinking abstractly and planning,
sentences.zh: 那么，如果你把所有时间都用来占用你有限的抽象思维和计划资源，

sentences.en: focusing on this one negative thing or several negative things that, that then basically tunes out other important areas of your life
sentences.zh: 专注于这一件负面事情或几件负面事情，那基本上就会屏蔽掉你生活中其他重要的领域，

sentences.en: where you might want to, um, use your, your mind, your problem solving capacity.
sentences.zh: 在这些领域你可能想要，嗯，使用你的头脑，你的解决问题的能力。

sentences.en: And so it can affect our decision-making.
sentences.zh: 所以它会影响我们的决策。

sentences.en: Like imagine, for example, have you ever had the experience of trying to read a book?
sentences.zh: 比如想象一下，你有没有过试图读书的经历？

sentences.en: When you're ruminating about a problem, like when that happens, many people report anecdotally, not being able to focus because these other negative thoughts are intruding in.
sentences.zh: 当你正在为一个问题反刍时，当这种情况发生时，许多人轶事式地报告说无法集中注意力，因为这些其他的负面想法正在侵入。

sentences.en: So it can really distract us from being good listeners or doing the jobs that we have at work or at school.
sentences.zh: 所以它真的会让我们分心，无法成为好的倾听者，或者无法做好我们在工作或学校里的工作。

sentences.en: And then finally, it can interfere with our relationships because one of the things we know about people,
sentences.zh: 最后，它会干扰我们的人际关系，因为关于人们，我们知道的一件事是，

sentences.en: when they experience, uh, heightened levels of inner voice run amok, so to speak, they tend to want to verbalize and talk about it to other people to get social support.
sentences.zh: 当他们经历，呃，内心声音失控加剧时，可以说，他们倾向于想要表达出来并与他人谈论它以获得社会支持。

sentences.en: And that's a great instinct.
sentences.zh: 这是一种很好的本能。

sentences.en: But what often happens is because these experiences are chronic, right?
sentences.zh: 但经常发生的情况是，因为这些经历是慢性的，对吧？

sentences.en: The, the inner voice is running on overdrive.
sentences.zh: 内心声音正在超速运转。

sentences.en: The inner critic maybe is taking over.
sentences.zh: 内心批评者可能正在接管。

sentences.en: Or then they keep talking about it over and over and over again.
sentences.zh: 或者他们不断地一遍又一遍地谈论它。

sentences.en: And that, that can actually push those we love away.
sentences.zh: 这实际上可能会把我们所爱的人推开。

sentences.en: And so, um, so it can be not very good for us when the inner voice runs awry.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，当内心声音出错时，这对我们来说可能不太好。

sentences.en: So you're director of your university's emotion and self-control lab.
sentences.zh: 你是你们大学情绪与自我控制实验室的主任。

sentences.en: And in your lab, you've done research on rumination and you've said that self-distancing can help.
sentences.zh: 在你的实验室里，你做过关于反刍的研究，你说过自我疏离（self-distancing）会有帮助。

sentences.en: Can you explain what self-distancing is and how you can do this when something upsetting happens?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下什么是自我疏离，以及当发生令人不安的事情时，你该如何做到这一点吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And so self-distancing is the ability to essentially focus on your, yourself from a more objective, psychologically removed perspective, uh, to illustrate why it matters.
sentences.zh: 自我疏离本质上是一种能力，即从一个更客观、心理上抽离的角度来关注你自己，呃，为了说明它为什么重要，

sentences.en: Um, I usually ask people to think of a time when a friend or loved one came to them with a problem that they were ruminating about or worried excessively about.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我通常请人们回想一下，当朋友或亲人带着他们正在反刍或过度担忧的问题来找他们时的情况。

sentences.en: And the problem wasn't really relative to them, just their friend.
sentences.zh: 这个问题与他们自己无关，只是关于他们的朋友。

sentences.en: In these situations, most people report being able to easily coach their friends through their problems, give them advice about what they should do, how they should act and
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，大多数人报告说能够轻松地指导朋友解决他们的问题，给他们关于应该做什么、应该如何行动的建议，以及

sentences.en: so forth.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。

sentences.en: And I would argue, and there's lots of data to support this, that the reason for that is because the problem is not happening to you, right?
sentences.zh: 我会说，而且有大量数据支持这一点，原因在于这个问题不是发生在你身上，对吧？

sentences.en: So you have psychological distance from that experience.
sentences.zh: 所以你与那种经历保持了心理距离。

sentences.en: And as a result, you're capable of thinking about it more objectively.
sentences.zh: 因此，你能够更客观地思考它。

sentences.en: What we've learned about human beings is that we, we have evolved to possess different psychological hacks, if you will, for providing us with distance from our own probleMs.
sentences.zh: 我们对人类的了解是，我们进化出了不同的心理技巧，如果你愿意的话，可以为我们提供与自身问题的距离。

sentences.en: And that's meant, that's what we've studied in the lab.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在实验室里研究的内容。

sentences.en: What are these different tools that people, uh, possess to get some mental space from the
sentences.zh: 人们拥有哪些不同的工具，呃，来从他们正在经历的问题中获得一些心理空间，

sentences.en: problems that they're experiencing so that they can think about them more similar to how they might think about another person's probleMs.
sentences.zh: 以便他们能以类似于思考他人问题的方式来思考自己的问题。

sentences.en: And one important tool that we've, we've studied along those lines is language is the inner voice.
sentences.zh: 我们研究过的一个重要工具是语言，即内心声音。

sentences.en: So in a certain sense, there are ways of using the inner voice to combat the toxic inner voice when it runs away.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种意义上，有一些方法可以使用内心声音来对抗失控的有毒内心声音。

sentences.en: And one of those tools is something we call distance self-talk, uh, which involves using
sentences.zh: 其中一个工具就是我们所说的“疏离式自言自语”（distance self-talk），呃，它涉及使用

sentences.en: your own name or other non first person pronouns, words like you or he or she to, to think about
sentences.zh: 你自己的名字或其他非第一人称代词，比如“你”、“他”或“她”这样的词，来思考

sentences.en: your life when you're experiencing problematic, uh, rumination or anxiety provoking experiences.
sentences.zh: 当你经历有问题、呃，引发焦虑的经历时，你的生活。

sentences.en: So if I'm really worried about making a good impression on you during this podcast, instead of thinking, what am I going to say?
sentences.zh: 所以如果我真的很担心在这个播客中给你留下好印象，而不是想：我要说什么？

sentences.en: And, and, and, uh, why, why am I going to say that?
sentences.zh: 以及，以及，呃，我为什么要说那个？

sentences.en: I might think, well, what is Ethan going to say?
sentences.zh: 我可能会想，好吧，伊森（Ethan）要说什么？

sentences.en: And why is Ethan going to say that?
sentences.zh: 伊森为什么要说那个？

sentences.en: And what we find is that that subtle shift from I to using your own name promotes distance and helps people think about experiences in a, in a more healthy and ultimately adaptive
sentences.zh: 我们发现，从“我”转变为使用你自己的名字，这种微妙的转变促进了距离感，并帮助人们以一种更健康、最终更具适应性的方式思考经历。

sentences.en: way.
sentences.zh: 方式。

sentences.en: And I'll just add one more point.
sentences.zh: 我再补充一点。

sentences.en: You know, the reason we think that this is so effective is because if you think about the context in which we use names, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们认为这之所以如此有效，是因为如果你想想我们使用名字的情境，对吧？

sentences.en: Most of the time we use names when we think about or refer to other people, right?
sentences.zh: 大多数时候，当我们思考或提到别人时，我们会使用名字，对吧？

sentences.en: Like 99% of the time we use names or thinking about referring to another person.
sentences.zh: 比如99%的时间我们使用名字是在思考或提到另一个人。

sentences.en: And so the idea is that when you use a name to refer to yourself, it's almost like this little psychological jujitsu move where you're getting yourself to think about yourself like
sentences.zh: 所以观点是，当你用名字来指代自己时，这就像是一种小小的心理柔术，你让自己像对待别人一样思考自己。

sentences.en: you are someone else.
sentences.zh: 你就像是别人。

sentences.en: So you're, you're using language to change the way you're actually thinking about the self.
sentences.zh: 所以你正在使用语言来改变你实际思考自我的方式。

sentences.en: So, so, so that's distance self-talk in a nutshell.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以，所以这就是简而言之的疏离式自言自语。

sentences.en: That's great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: It sounds, I've never even thought about that as a way to, if you, you know, think of yourself
sentences.zh: 听起来，我甚至从未想过这是一种方法，如果你，你知道，在经历充满挑战的时刻时，以第三人称思考自己，

sentences.en: in the third person as you're going through a challenging time, because you can also, again,
sentences.zh: 因为你也可以，再次，

sentences.en: treat yourself as though you would treat a friend, because you likely would treat a friend or family member, you know, loved one better than you might talk to yourself in a lot of
sentences.zh: 像对待朋友一样对待自己，因为你很可能会比在很多情况下对自己说话的方式更好地对待朋友或家人，你知道，所爱的人。

sentences.en: cases.
sentences.zh: 案例。

sentences.en: So are there other distancing strategies you can employ when needed?
sentences.zh: 那么，在需要时还有其他可以采用的疏离策略吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there, there, there, there's a whole toolbox of distancing strategies that exiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，有，有，有，有一个完整的疏离策略工具箱存在。

sentences.en: Another, another one that is empirically validated and I find personally find useful is to imagine how you're going to feel a week or a month or a year later, right?
sentences.zh: 另一个，另一个经过实证验证的，我个人觉得有用的策略是想象你一周、一个月或一年后会有什么感觉，对吧？

sentences.en: So it's something called temporal distancing.
sentences.zh: 所以这被称为时间疏离（temporal distancing）。

sentences.en: It's kind of like a mental time travel where oftentimes we get so consumed with what is happening in the moment.
sentences.zh: 这有点像心理时间旅行，因为我们往往太沉迷于当下发生的事情。

sentences.en: We forget that with time things change and, and actually oftentimes things get better.
sentences.zh: 我们忘记了随着时间的推移事情会发生变化，而且，实际上往往事情会变得更好。

sentences.en: And so if you find yourself ruminating about something, you might think, well, how am I going to feel about this a year from now or 10 years from now?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你发现自己在为某事反刍，你可能会想，好吧，一年后或十年后我对这件事会有什么感觉？

sentences.en: That's another kind of distancing hack.
sentences.zh: 这是另一种疏离技巧。

sentences.en: There's some work showing that writing expressively about your, your experiences.
sentences.zh: 有一些研究表明，通过写作来表达你的经历。

sentences.en: So doing something like journaling is also something that has been shown to be effective for helping people cope with negative experiences.
sentences.zh: 所以做一些像写日记这样的事情，也被证明对帮助人们应对负面经历是有效的。

sentences.en: And one pathway through which it works, not the only one, um, but one has to do with distance, right?
sentences.zh: 它起作用的途径之一，不是唯一的，嗯，但其中一个与距离有关，对吧？

sentences.en: So when you're writing about your own experiences, you're becoming the target, right?
sentences.zh: 所以当你写下自己的经历时，你成为了目标，对吧？

sentences.en: Like you're thinking about yourself as this character in a play that is your life.
sentences.zh: 就像你把自己想象成你生活中那部戏里的角色。

sentences.en: And so there's a distance and quality that writing about one's experiences, uh, can also have.
sentences.zh: 所以写作关于一个人的经历，也可能有一种距离感和品质。

sentences.en: And so those are just a couple of examples there, you know, there are quite a few more that exist that, um, you know, you can read about in various places.
sentences.zh: 所以这些只是其中的几个例子，你知道，还有相当多其他的存在，嗯，你知道，你可以在各种地方读到它们。

sentences.en: I'm happy to refer people to sources if that'd be helpful.
sentences.zh: 如果对大家有帮助的话，我很乐意为大家提供一些参考资料。

sentences.en: We can touch on that a bit at the end.
sentences.zh: 我们可以在最后稍微谈谈这一点。

sentences.en: So you also research social rejection and emotional pain.
sentences.zh: 所以，你也在研究社会排斥和情感痛苦。

sentences.en: Um, why and how does something emotional cause physical pain?
sentences.zh: 嗯，为什么以及如何某种情感会引起身体上的疼痛呢？

sentences.en: Great question.
sentences.zh: 问得好。

sentences.en: And, uh, yeah, we have done some work looking at, you know, there's this curious phenomenon where people who find themselves ostracized or excommunicated or just rejected from work
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，我们做过一些研究，你知道，有一个有趣的现象：那些发现自己被排挤、被驱逐，或者仅仅是被工作场所拒绝的人，

sentences.en: or in love do this seemingly strange thing.
sentences.zh: 或者在爱情中被拒绝的人，会做出这种看似奇怪的行为。

sentences.en: They use this language of physical pain to talk about their experience.
sentences.zh: 他们用身体疼痛的语言来描述自己的经历。

sentences.en: They say, my feelings are hurt.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我的心受到了伤害。

sentences.en: I'm in pain.
sentences.zh: 我感到很痛苦。

sentences.en: And so that, that has been curious, a curious kind of phenomenon for many of us in the field.
sentences.zh: 所以，这对我们领域里的许多人来说，一直是一种令人好奇的现象。

sentences.en: Like why would a person use words that are normally specific to the experience of physical pain to describe this emotional experience?
sentences.zh: 为什么一个人会用通常专门描述身体疼痛的词汇来描述这种情感体验呢？

sentences.en: And one idea has to do with the fact that because our social relationships are so absolutely central to our ability to succeed and thrive in this world, right?
sentences.zh: 其中一个想法与这样一个事实有关：因为我们的社会关系对于我们在这个世界上成功和繁荣的能力来说是绝对核心的，对吧？

sentences.en: Human beings, we are a social species.
sentences.zh: 人类，我们是一个社会性物种。

sentences.en: We thrive on these social relationships that we have evolved in ways that we need really powerful cues that alert us to danger when those social ties are severed.
sentences.zh: 我们依赖这些社会关系而繁荣，我们进化的方式使我们需要非常强有力的信号，在这些社会纽带断裂时提醒我们危险。

sentences.en: And one of the best systems that exist for warning us of potential danger is pain, right?
sentences.zh: 而现有的警告我们潜在危险的最佳系统之一就是疼痛，对吧？

sentences.en: If we go to touch a stove and we, we sense heat, we instantly pull back our hand.
sentences.zh: 如果我们去摸炉子，感觉到热，我们会立刻缩回手。

sentences.en: And so the idea is that within human beings, we make use of the physical pain system that exists.
sentences.zh: 所以这个想法是，在人类内部，我们利用了现有的身体疼痛系统。

sentences.en: It's a very primitive system for alerting us to danger and getting us to quickly respond as a result.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常原始的系统，用于提醒我们危险，并促使我们迅速做出反应。

sentences.en: And so we rely on that, that system when we experience potentially socially threatening experiences.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们经历潜在的社会威胁性事件时，我们会依赖那个系统。

sentences.en: Does that make sense?
sentences.zh: 这说得通吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it does.
sentences.zh: 是的，说得通。

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And how can people better cope with rejection?
sentences.zh: 那么人们该如何更好地应对拒绝呢？

sentences.en: Well, you know, there are many of the, the, the tools that exist for coping with negative experiences more generally, like experiences that might cause you to feel anxiety or anger
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，有很多现有的工具可以用来应对更广泛的负面经历，比如那些可能让你感到焦虑或愤怒的经历，

sentences.en: or sadness also apply to coping with rejection.
sentences.zh: 或者悲伤，这些也适用于应对拒绝。

sentences.en: So some of the distancing tools that we've already talked about, uh, I think would be useful for coping with rejection.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们之前谈到的一些疏离工具，我认为对于应对拒绝也是有用的。

sentences.en: And there's some data to support that there are also, of course, like leveraging our social relationships with other people.
sentences.zh: 有一些数据支持这一点，当然，还有利用我们与他人的社会关系。

sentences.en: So finding people to talk about our problems who are skilled in helping us, uh, see the bigger picture, not getting stuck in the details.
sentences.zh: 所以，寻找那些善于帮助我们看待大局、而不是陷入细节的人来倾诉我们的问题。

sentences.en: So, so oftentimes you go to other people for help and they don't actually help you because in their attempts to be supportive, they end up just getting you to think through what,
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，你去找别人寻求帮助，但他们并没有真正帮到你，因为在他们试图提供支持的过程中，他们最终只是让你反复思考，

sentences.en: how awful you feel as a result.
sentences.zh: 结果让你感觉有多糟糕。

sentences.en: So to make it concrete, let's say you're rejected because, oh my God, I can't believe you were just rejected.
sentences.zh: 为了具体一点，假设你被拒绝了，因为，天哪，我不敢相信你竟然被拒绝了。

sentences.en: You must feel awful.
sentences.zh: 你一定感觉糟透了。

sentences.en: I'm so sorry.
sentences.zh: 我真为你难过。

sentences.en: Where did it happen?
sentences.zh: 是在哪里发生的？

sentences.en: What happened?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？

sentences.en: So in, in my attempt to connect with you, I am essentially just getting you to think over and over about to rehearse the negative features of, of your experience.
sentences.zh: 所以，在我试图与你建立联系的过程中，我本质上只是让你反复思考，去重温你经历中的负面特征。

sentences.en: And, and that can be not so helpful longterm.
sentences.zh: 而从长远来看，这可能并不是很有帮助。

sentences.en: So there's some evidence that what makes, what makes like really good social support is when
sentences.zh: 所以有一些证据表明，什么才是真正好的社会支持，那就是当你

sentences.en: you go to someone else, they're capable of connecting with you and showing that you, that they care.
sentences.zh: 去找别人时，他们能够与你建立联系，并表现出他们在乎你。

sentences.en: So they learn a little bit about what you're going through, but then they really shift to trying to help you put the experience in perspective, right?
sentences.zh: 所以他们会了解一点你正在经历的事情，但随后他们会真正转向试图帮助你从全局角度看待这段经历，对吧？

sentences.en: So, well, you know what?
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，你知道吗？

sentences.en: They're more fish in the sea, right?
sentences.zh: 天涯何处无芳草，对吧？

sentences.en: Like that's, that's the cliche, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是陈词滥调，对吧？

sentences.en: Or, or let's look at the big picture.
sentences.zh: 或者，让我们看看大局。

sentences.en: You know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: Two years from now, things are going to look different.
sentences.zh: 两年后，情况看起来就会不同了。

sentences.en: So in a certain sense, other people can be tools that help give us more space, more perspective, more distance.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，其他人可以成为帮助我们获得更多空间、更多视角、更多距离的工具。

sentences.en: And so that's another thing that people can do.
sentences.zh: 所以这是人们可以做的另一件事。

sentences.en: And there are boatloads of other, other techniques and, and, and, and tools that exist for helping
sentences.zh: 还有大量的其他技术和工具可以帮助

sentences.en: people manage rumination that, um, you know, nature is, is one, um, that has been recently quite extensively studied.
sentences.zh: 人们管理反刍思维，嗯，你知道，大自然就是其中之一，嗯，最近被研究得相当广泛。

sentences.en: There are, um, religious rituals that people engage in that can be, or, or even non-religious rituals that can be helpful.
sentences.zh: 有一些人们参与的宗教仪式，或者甚至是非宗教仪式，都可能是有帮助的。

sentences.en: So, um, so that's really a, a, a huge question with lots of, we would probably need a lot more time to, to get into all those techniques in depth.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，这是一个非常大的问题，我们可能需要更多的时间来深入探讨所有这些技术。

sentences.en: But you've offered a lot of great tips in terms of, you know, how to handle rumination, rejection, those things that just, that just happen.
sentences.zh: 但你已经提供了很多很棒的建议，关于如何处理反刍思维、拒绝，那些只是，只是发生的事情。

sentences.en: Um, I think most people can say that those things have happened in their lives at some point.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想大多数人都可以说这些事情在他们生命中的某个时刻发生过。

sentences.en: Um, I want to turn out to some other work you do in your lab.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想转到你在实验室所做的其他一些工作。

sentences.en: Um, and you've done some research on social networking sites and wellbeing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你做了一些关于社交网站和幸福感的研究。

sentences.en: And in a paper you published, you asked that very question that's on the minds of many today.
sentences.zh: 在你发表的一篇论文中，你提出了今天许多人心中所想的那个问题。

sentences.en: Um, does social media make us feel better or worse?
sentences.zh: 嗯，社交媒体让我们感觉更好还是更糟？

sentences.en: Uh, what did you find?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你发现了什么？

sentences.en: So what we find is that, um, so when you, when you use social media in a particular way, it predicts a decline in how good people feel.
sentences.zh: 我们发现的是，嗯，当你以特定的方式使用社交媒体时，它预示着人们感觉变差。

sentences.en: And in particular, when people passively use social media, meaning that they log into their
sentences.zh: 特别是，当人们被动地使用社交媒体时，意味着他们登录他们的

sentences.en: social media sites, we've studied primarily Facebook and they browse what's happening in their
sentences.zh: 社交媒体网站，我们主要研究的是 Facebook，他们浏览社交媒体世界里正在发生的事情，

sentences.en: social media universe, um, that tends to lead people to feel, uh, envy feelings of envy, which in turn predicts declines and how good they feel.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这往往会导致人们感到嫉妒，而这反过来又预示着他们感觉变差。

sentences.en: And how, how we think all of this works is, is as follows.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这一切是如何运作的，如下所示。

sentences.en: We know that people are motivated to present themselves flatteringly in the eyes of others.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，人们有动力在他人眼中展示自己讨人喜欢的一面。

sentences.en: We all do it all the time, not just on social media, but in the offline world as well.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人一直都在这样做，不仅是在社交媒体上，在现实世界中也是如此。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I wake up, I, I usually, if I know I'm going to see other people, I shave, I comb my hair, I put on a shirt that's not ripped and stained.
sentences.zh: 所以我醒来，我，如果我知道我要见别人，我通常会刮胡子，梳头，穿上一件没有破损和污渍的衬衫。

sentences.en: And I do that because I want to convey a particular impression.
sentences.zh: 我这样做是因为我想传达一种特定的印象。

sentences.en: Um, but there are limits to how that impression management process works in the offline world, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是这种印象管理过程在现实世界中是有局限性的，对吧？

sentences.en: Like I can comb my hair and shave, but you know, the hair got, can get messed up and maybe I nick myself when I'm shaving when there's nothing I can really do about that.
sentences.zh: 比如我可以梳头和刮胡子，但你知道，头发可能会乱，也许我刮胡子时会割伤自己，对此我真的无能为力。

sentences.en: Well, when you transition to the social media universe, things change quite dramatically, our ability to curate the way we present ourselves goes on hyperdrive.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当你进入社交媒体世界时，情况发生了巨大的变化，我们策划自己展示方式的能力进入了超速状态。
